A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL experiments, benchmark comparisons, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix G, including Atari, Craftax, and multi-agent results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional normalization comparisons and an experiment with highly random data collection in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The reported Craftax recurrent architecture changes from a GRU in v1 Appendix F to an LSTM in v2 Appendix D. Algorithms 1–2, Q(lambda), and VDN integration remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the architecture revision reflects rerunning experiments or correcting the description.

E1.justification: The same benchmark coverage is retained: Atari, MinAtar, Craftax, Hanabi, Smax, Overcooked, classic control, Baird's counterexample, and DeepSea. DeepSea and the Dopamine Atari configuration already appear in v1's appendix. The new high-exploration experiment uses existing Atari-10 tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds BatchNorm and CrossQ-style PQN variants to the Atari comparisons in Figures 5a and 12. Removing v1 Table 4 eliminates the detailed Hanabi score comparison with R2D2-VDN, although the R2D2 resource comparison remains in Table 2.

E3.justification: The new Atari experiment collects data with randomness decreasing from 100% to 70% (v2 Figure 13). Normalization experiments introduce additional controls, and the reported Craftax recurrent module changes from GRU to LSTM. Retained benchmark budgets and hyperparameter tables otherwise remain substantially unchanged; these revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analysis of the central normalization mechanism: Atari ablations add BatchNorm and CrossQ-style modifications, while Craftax explicitly compares three normalization choices with and without input normalization. Figure 13 additionally tests learning under highly off-policy sampling. Existing Baird, DeepSea, lambda, and replay-buffer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Table 4 removes explicit Hanabi numerical uncertainty entries, including PQN-VDN's 24.37±0.04. Both versions retain the stated practice of 10 seeds generally and 3 for ALE, along with shaded learning curves. No increase in repeated runs or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds normalization-variant results and shows a learned policy outperforming its highly random behavior policy. It removes the detailed Hanabi mean, maximum, and training-time entries from v1 Table 4. The ALE summary in Table 3 and all 57 per-game score pairs in v1 Table 11/v2 Table 9 are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes the BatchNorm-myopia theorem and proof, adds a mean-square TD convergence theorem and Markov-sampling analysis, and introduces explicit Robbins–Monro, compactness, Lipschitz, and geometric-ergodicity assumptions. It also revises the LayerNorm stability theorem and analyzed critic: v1 applies ReLU after LayerNorm, whereas v2 applies LayerNorm after a general Lipschitz activation. Appendix B contains substantive new and rewritten derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces BatchNorm-induced myopia as a principal theoretical contribution with a general TD stability analysis. The headline Hanabi comparison against R2D2 is also withdrawn in favor of MAPPO-focused discussion. The central proposal of fast, regularized Q-learning without target networks or replay remains.

C2.justification: v1 explains BatchNorm failures through myopia and short effective horizons. v2 instead emphasizes the gap between naive BatchNorm and practical CrossQ modifications, acknowledges beneficial input normalization, and calls for further theoretical analysis. It also clarifies why online PQN remains off-policy and interprets the new highly random sampling experiment accordingly.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement directing readers to an anonymous repository instead of v1's named public repository. It removes the Craftax MLP hyperparameter table while retaining the MLP results. Hardware, optimizer information, pseudocode, and the remaining hyperparameter values are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial positioning against Yue et al.'s LayerNorm analysis, expands distinctions from asynchronous Q-learning and CrossQ, and adds references supporting its theoretical assumptions and Retrace discussion. The detailed PQL and large-batch discussion in v1 Appendix B.4 disappears. These changes extend beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The theoretical narrative is reorganized around TD stability, LayerNorm stabilization, and a revised BatchNorm discussion. Related work and experimental interpretations are extensively rewritten; preliminary sections are reordered, appendices reorganized, a reproducibility section added, and the broader-impact section removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, merges the separate Craftax and multi-agent figures, expands normalization panels and per-game Atari plots, and adds the high-exploration figure. It also removes the Hanabi results and Craftax MLP hyperparameter tables and substantially rearranges appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The added normalization controls and highly off-policy test strengthen empirical diagnosis, and the BatchNorm discussion becomes more qualified. However, the new Appendix B.1 proof does not justify its inference from vanishing weighted-average error in Eq. (11) to iterate convergence. Removing detailed Hanabi comparisons and uncertainty, plus Craftax MLP settings, also reduces transparency. These material benefits and unresolved theoretical and reporting costs prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
